plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-attachment-library · Attachment library

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds **Settings → Attachment library**: every image and file attachment stored on this machine, the space it takes, and which conversations still use it (active, archived, moving to the trash, or in the trash).

**Read-only.** Nothing is deleted: the plugin never creates, changes, moves, or deletes an attachment, a session log, a trash file, or a cache entry; "Show in Finder" only selects a file and never opens or runs it. The plugin's only write is the read-only copy "Open in Preview" places in the system temporary directory (outside DSH data), removed when the plugin stops. Its purpose is to check the reference counts before any cleanup is considered.

- DSH 0.2.x (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`, including the 0.2.1 alpha previews)
- Trash statistics work with [`dsh-plugin-session-trash`](https://github.com/ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-session-trash); without it only existing conversations are counted

## Install

**Desktop**: open **Plugins** in the sidebar → **Add plugin**, enter one of the following, click **Install**, then **Enable now** (new plugins start disabled):

- GitHub: `https://github.com/ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-attachment-library`, or a version such as `github:ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-attachment-library#v0.4.1`
- npm: `dsh-plugin-attachment-library`
- An absolute path to a local package, for example `/path/to/dsh-plugin-attachment-library-0.4.1.tgz` (made with `pnpm pack`)

Do not enter the source directory: its `node_modules` holds development copies of DSH packages that conflict with DSH's own.

**Command line** (optional): quit DSH, then run `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-attachment-library`.

**Uninstall**: uninstall "Attachment library" on the **Plugins** page. The plugin stores no data; attachments are not affected.

## What the page shows

- **Totals**: all attachments (count and size); images and files; used by existing conversations, used only by conversations in the trash, and not used by any conversation (count and size each); attachments referenced but missing from the store; the size of the regenerable resize cache.
- **List**: a type icon (an image icon for images, an icon by extension for files), type, file names (every name stored for the same content), size, image dimensions and format, store time, and each referencing conversation with its title and status. An attachment shared by several conversations lists all of them.
- **Open in Preview** (macOS only): an arrow icon button on stored image rows (tooltip "Open in Preview") opens the image in Preview on the Host. Preview gets a read-only copy with the right extension, not DSH's own file (see below). File rows have no such button.
- **Show in Finder**: a folder icon button at the right of each stored row (tooltip "Show in Finder") selects the file in the Host's Finder (Windows Explorer, or the default Linux file manager): a file attachment shows under its real file name, an image as its content-named object file. It appears only when the page talks to the local DSH, the Host has a desktop file manager, and DSH allows desktop handoff; a failure is shown under the row.
- **Rescan**: the refresh icon button at the top right (tooltip "Rescan"); it is disabled while a scan runs, and "Rescanning…" is shown.
- **Filters**: type (all / images / files) and references (all / existing / trash only / unused); **sort** by time or by size (newest or largest first). The list shows 100 rows at a time.
- **Incomplete logs**: session logs that could not be read in full (damaged, cut short) are listed with a note that the "unused" counts may be too high.

## Why Finder shows no preview for images

DSH stores each image under its SHA-256 digest (for example `attachments/v1/objects/3f/3f9a…`) with **no file extension**, read-only (0400). The content is an ordinary normalized JPEG, WebP, PNG, or GIF, not encrypted; macOS decides the file type from the extension, so Finder shows no thumbnail and a double-click does not open it as an image. File attachments differ: each also has a read-only hard link under its real file name, which Finder shows normally.

## Counting rules

| Rule | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Identity | DSH stores attachments once per content digest (SHA-256); images and files are stored separately, so the same bytes stored as an image and as a file are two rows |
| References | Every `{ type: 'image' \| 'file', attachment: { attachmentId } }` in a session log counts: user prompts, tool results, and system messages |
| Conversations | A subagent session's references count for the conversation that started it; a fork is its own conversation (it inherits its parent's prefix, so both are listed) |
| Existing conversations | Every session the session backend lists, read through the official read-only handle; status active, archived, or moving to the trash |
| Trash | Logs inside the trash directory are read directly (raw JSONL or Zstandard frames); the title is the one recorded when the conversation was moved |
| In use / trash only / unused | Any conversation outside the trash (including one waiting to move) makes it "in use"; only trashed conversations make it "trash only"; none makes it "unused" |
| Size | Each image object and file object counts once; file names are hard links and take no extra space; missing attachments add no size |
| Store time | The modification time of the stored object (when this content was first stored) |

## Cache

The first scan reads every session log and can be slow with many logs. After that:

- existing sessions are read again only when the session backend's revision changed;
- trashed sessions are read again only when the log file's device, inode, size, or modification time changed;
- image dimensions are cached by the same file facts.

The cache lives in the DSH process memory only and is never written to disk; the first scan after a DSH restart reads every log again.

## Configuration

Every DSH directory is only read.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `attachmentDirectory` | `<DSH home>/attachments/v1` | Attachment store; set it when `dsh-attachment-local` has its own `dshHome` |
| `trashDirectory` | `<DSH home>/session-trash` | Session trash; keep it equal to `dsh-plugin-session-trash`'s `trashDirectory` |
| `requestCacheDirectory` | `<DSH home>/cache/attachments/request-images` | Regenerable per-model resize cache; only its size is measured |
| `previewDirectory` | system temporary directory | Where the private temporary directory for "Open in Preview" copies is created; the only place the plugin writes |

## How "Show in Finder" works

- It uses DSH's own capability: the Host calls `revealNativePath` from the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command` (`open -R` on macOS, Explorer `/select` on Windows, the containing directory on Linux), the same function behind DSH's built-in reveal actions. Availability uses the same checks (`nativeFileManager()`, `canOpenNativePath()`); the browser also requires `ctx.remote.$host.isLoopback` and follows DSH's `session.canOpenWorkspacePath()` switch.
- The official `session.openWorkspacePath` is not reused directly: it takes an absolute path from the browser and only accepts paths mapped into the workspace filesystem, which the attachment store is not.
- The browser sends only the attachment kind and id (`sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits); the authenticated `/api` gateway validates them strictly and rejects any extra field, a path included.
- The Host derives the path from the id: a file is `attachments/v1/files/<prefix>/<digest>/<name>` (the first name in sorted order, or the `file-objects` object when none exists), an image `attachments/v1/objects/<prefix>/<sha256>`. The target must be a plain file inside the attachment store with no symbolic link on the way; anything else is "not found".

## How "Open in Preview" works

- The browser sends only the image id (`sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex digits); the gateway validates it strictly and rejects any extra field, a path included. The Host finds `attachments/v1/objects/<prefix>/<sha256>` and requires a plain file i

plugins.description: Codex-style Create Workspace dialog for DeepSeek Harness: type a name and the folder is created for you, or pick a folder with a native chooser that remembers where you were.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-create-dialog

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **Create Workspace** dialog for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type a name and go, or pick a folder with a chooser that finally remembers where you were.

![The Create Workspace dialog: a name field, a workspace folder row with a Choose folder button, and a New workspace location row with a Change button](docs/create-workspace.png)

## What it does

Clicking **Add workspace…** in DSH today opens the OS folder dialog immediately. This plugin replaces that with a small dialog that asks two independent questions: what is the workspace called, and where does it live. Answer the first only and it creates the folder for you; answer the second and the folder you picked *is* the workspace.

| You do | You get |
| --- | --- |
| Type a name, press **Create** | A new folder with that name is created under **New workspace location**, registered as a workspace, and a session opens in it |
| Click **Choose folder…** | The native Windows folder dialog, starting **where you left off**, not at some default |
| Choose a folder, leave the name empty | The name fills itself in from the folder's own name |
| Choose a folder, having typed a name | Your name wins — the workspace is registered, then renamed to it |
| Click **Change…** on New workspace location | Pick where name-only workspaces go from now on; the choice is saved and survives restarts |
| Cancel / Esc / click the backdrop | Nothing happens — no folder, no registration |

### The effect, before and after

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating `my-project` | Create the folder in Explorer first, then hunt for it in the picker | Type `my-project`. Done |
| The folder picker's starting point | The OS default, every single time | The directory you last chose |
| Where new workspaces land | Wherever you navigate to | A location you set once, visible in the dialog, changeable any time |
| Naming a workspace after its folder | Retype the folder name | Auto-filled |

## Install

### From the DSH UI (simplest)

Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, paste this address, click **Install**, then **Enable now**:

```text
https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
```

That box takes a package name, a Git address, a tarball or a local absolute path. A repository URL works because this package ships a `dsh.bundle` patch — DSH checks exactly that before it installs. Restart DeepSeek Harness if the plugin does not come up.

Two things worth knowing: it downloads straight from GitHub, so GitHub has to be reachable (the China-mirror option only covers registry packages, not repository downloads); and DSH does not auto-update third-party plugins yet — upgrading means uninstall + install again.

> Already installed with `tools/install.mjs` below? Run `node tools/install.mjs --uninstall` first, so the profile does not end up with two loader rows for the same id.

### One-line prompt for your agent

If you would rather not click through it:

```text
Install the DSH plugin at https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog into my DSH and tell me when to restart.
```

### From the plugin market (once listed)

Search for **dsh-workspace-create-dialog** in [dshmarket](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) and install it in one click. The listing is [pending a PR](contrib/awesome-dsh-plugin/) to [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) (their CI requires the repository to be at least one day old); until it lands, use the routes above and below.

### Manual install from this repository

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
cd dsh-workspace-create-dialog
node tools/install.mjs
```

That copies the package into your DSH profile's `node_modules` and appends one loader line to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. It resolves your DSH home the same way the harness does — explicit config, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh`.

**Then restart DeepSeek Harness** (the host half is a Node module, so a config reload alone will not import it). After that, changing `lib/client.js` only needs a page refresh; changing `lib/index.js` still needs a restart.

`node tools/install.mjs --dry-run` prints what it would do without writing anything; `--uninstall` removes the package and its loader row again.

Publishing to npm is **not** required: the market installs from GitHub exactly the same way, and listing is unaffected either way.

## How it works

### It uses the official extension point, not a patch

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` declares a `single` slot where the "pick a directory" step is handed to whichever plugin fills it:

```text
sidebar.workspaces.directoryFlow              ← the sidebar's "Add workspace…"
conversation.hero.workspace.directoryFlow     ← the empty-state entry
```

The owner hands the occupant the whole interaction contract:

```ts
interface DirectoryFlowOwnerProps {
  open: boolean                     // a pick is requested
  busy: boolean                     // the owner is adopting the picked path
  onPicked: (path: string) => void  // report the directory; the owner registers it and opens a session
  onCancel: () => void
  onError: (message: string) => void
}
```

This plugin registers its own occupant into both slots at **priority -100**. A `single` slot renders the lowest-priority entry, the shipped native driver sits at `0`, so this dialog wins (two entries at the *same* priority throw, which is the official protection against ambiguity). Removing the loader line from your profile patch restores the stock behaviour exactly.

### Why the folder dialog is built here instead of reused

The desktop app opens its folder dialog from the Electron main process without a starting directory:

```js
// D:\App\DSH\resources\app.asar → lib/main.js
dialog.showOpenDialog(window, { properties: ['openDirectory', 'createDirectory'] })
```

There is no `defaultPath`, which is exactly why the chooser always starts in the same place. A plugin cannot reach that call: the DSH host is a *child process* of Electron. So `lib/pick-folder.js` opens its own `IFileDialog` — a small C# COM interop compiled and run by the **Windows PowerShell 5.1 that ships with Windows**:

- **no dependencies**: no koffi, no PowerShell 7, no native module to publish;
- compilation happens **in memory** (~120 ms per call), so there is no DLL cache to corrupt or lock;
- the one line that matters is `IFileDialog::SetFolder` — the remembered directory as the starting point;
- the dialog runs in a child process, so a native fault cannot take the host down.

The C# method declaration order must match the COM vtable (`Show=3`, `SetOptions=9`, `SetFolder=12`, `SetTitle=17`, `GetResult=20`). Getting it wrong does not error — it just silently does the wrong thing — so a self-test asserts the order.

## Where name-only workspaces are created

The **New workspace location** is resolved in this order (`lib/base-dir.js`, a pure function):

1. **What you set in the dialog** — highest priority; once you change it, it is yours;
2. **`config.baseDir`** from your profile patch — the value used at install time;
3. **The root of your default workspace** — the parent of the workspace whose directory is named `default-workspace` (a name the harness fixes, independent of UI language). New workspaces land next to it. This is the default for a fresh install;
4. **Fallback** — `<Documents>/deepseek-harness`, or `<home>/deepseek-harness` when there is no Documents folder.

The resolved value is written to the state file, so "what it was on first run" is decided once and only you change it afterwards. `config.baseDir` is a seed, not an order.

## HTTP routes

All four are loopback-guarded (loopback socket + loopback `Host` + same-origin marker; `x-forwarded-for` is never trusted) — they create directories and open windows on the host machine, so nothing off-machine may reach them.

| Route | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/config` | GET | Current location + last directory |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/base-dir` | POST | `{"

plugins.description: GitMate — a smart Git panel for DeepSeek Harness: diffs, generated commit messages, a commit graph with rewind, and .gitignore generation, plus ten agent tools.
plugins.readme_text:
# GitMate

**A Git panel in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) sidebar — plus the same operations as fifteen agent tools.**

Runs anywhere the Harness does: macOS, Linux, and Windows (PowerShell).

Only two things genuinely differ across platforms, and both live on the Host side: **how arguments are quoted** (PowerShell doubles a single quote, a POSIX shell closes-escapes-reopens; chosen by `process.platform`) and **how the environment is passed** (through the shell request's `env` field rather than a POSIX `VAR=value` prefix, which is not a command on Windows). Nothing else is platform-aware: paths go through `node:path`, nothing outside `lib/` is written, and no file needing an executable bit is created. When the sandbox will not start, the advice **names the cause for the platform you are on** (bubblewrap/Landlock on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS, `%TEMP%` on Windows).

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Review changes, read diffs, stage, commit with a generated message, merge, stash, sync, and rewind history without leaving the panel. Every operation is also a tool the agent can call, so asking in chat works too.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:alanhaskey/dsh-gitmate
```

Restart DSH once, refresh the page, then open **GitMate** from the sidebar's **+** menu.

> The internal ids (Loader row `dsh-git`, tab key) differ from the package name on purpose: the row id is the key of a config row you may already have, and renaming it would orphan your saved settings.

## Reviewing and committing

- **Four groups** — conflicts, staged, changes, untracked. Each row shows the kind in words, the path, and that file's `+N −M`. Row actions stage, unstage, and discard, with a second click for anything destructive.
- **Diffs like an editor** — two line-number gutters, `+`/`−` markers, tinted rows, and only the changed span of a replaced line marked. Click a file to expand it in place; click again to collapse. Widen the context from 3 lines to 24 when a hunk needs more of the file.
- **One row of list actions**, shown only when they would do something, with the counts in the labels.
- **Amend** — fold the staged changes into the previous commit; leaving the message box empty keeps the existing message.
- **A draggable splitter** between the list and the commit card resizes the message box.
- **A panel that is working says so** — every operation shows a turning indicator and names itself ("Committing…", "Reviewing the staged changes…") instead of only greying its buttons out. It sits with the messages at the foot of the list, above the splitter, so it never covers the commit box.

## AI features

| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Commit message** | Generated from the staged diff. If you have already typed something, the button becomes *Refine draft*: the model keeps your intent and fills in the rest instead of replacing it. |
| **Review before commit** | Reads the staged changes and reports only what would bite — a wrong result, a missed edge case, an unhandled error, a committed secret, debug output left in, a behaviour change with no test. Click a finding to open that file's diff. |
| **Split this commit** | Divides the staged changes into commits that each stand on their own, with a message for each. The plan is a draft you can edit: rewrite any message, merge a group into the one above, remove one, ask for a new plan, commit one group at a time, or commit them all in order. Each commit leaves the other files staged. |
| **Explain a change** | Two to five bullets on what a file's change does, so you can review without reading every line. |
| **`.gitignore`** | Infers the rules from the project's manifests and layout. One button creates it; one adds what is missing **and tidies the whole file** — exact duplicates, rules an earlier broader rule already covers (`node_modules/.cache/` after `node_modules/`), and runs of blank lines. It groups entries under headings only when that cannot change the meaning: with a `!` rule (git decides by the last match, so order is semantic) or with your own comments, the order is kept and the panel says so. |

Buttons that call a model are marked **AI**. Every generation uses the session's default model — there is no second model to configure.

## Branches, history, remotes

- **Branch selector** — switch, create, delete, and merge any branch into the checked-out one. A conflicted merge is reported with the files that need a decision, and can be aborted.
- **Commit graph** — every branch and remote-tracking branch, not just this one. Expand a commit for its full message, the files it touched, and what you can do to it: rewind, revert, cherry-pick, rebase, or tag. Click a changed file to see its diff inside that commit.
- **Remotes** — push, pull, fetch, and a **Sync** that fetches, fast-forwards, then pushes. It refuses to merge a diverged branch rather than inventing a merge commit.
- **Stash** — set work aside and take it back later (pop, apply, drop).

## Setup

Without a repository the **history button is disabled** — there is no history to show — while **settings stays reachable**, because that is where someone looks when the panel is not doing what they expect. If the repository disappears while the panel is open (the folder changed, `.git` was removed), the view falls back to the change list rather than leaving the button lit on a view that cannot render.



One click initialises a repository and writes the local commit identity; two buttons handle `.gitignore`. Nothing is chosen from a list of ecosystems — the plugin reads the project and decides.

## Configuration

Settings live in this plugin's own row in `cordis.patch.yml`, so they survive upgrades and stay visible on the Plugins page. Everything below is a button or a checkbox; there is nothing to type unless you want custom instructions.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageLanguage` | `auto` | Language of generated text: `auto` (follow the repository), `en`, `zh`. When unset or `auto`, the panel's own messages read as Chinese. |
| `messageStyle` | `conventional` | `conventional` (`feat: …`) or `plain`. |
| `messageTemplate` | — | Extra instructions, appended last so they override the defaults. |
| `signoff` | `false` | Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer. |
| `defaultBranch` | `main` | Branch created by *Initialise*. |
| `maxPromptBytes` | `24000` | Diff text handed to the model per change set. |
| `maxDiffBytes` | `80000` | Patch text a tool returns before truncating. |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per git command; network commands get four times this. |

## Safety

- **Nothing destructive happens on a single click.** Discarding, deleting a branch, dropping a stash, rebasing, and rewinding all ask first, and say what will be lost.
- **Rewinding and reverting are separate**, because they are: rewinding moves the branch and rewrites history, reverting adds an inverse commit and is safe for anything already pushed. The panel warns before a rewind that would rewrite published history.
- **"Undo this commit" and "rewind to here" are separate too.** On the newest commit the button undoes that commit and leaves its changes staged, unstaged, or deleted as you choose; on an older commit it moves the branch pointer back to that commit. The notice names the commit that was actually undone and always states how many were discarded — including none.
- **A refusal says which mode refused.** A read-only session cannot write `.git`, so committing and switching branches are rejected by design; the message names the mode and what to switch to. If it is already `danger-full-access` and still refused, the sandbox backend on that machine is refusing writes and the Harness needs restarting — two different problems, told apart.
- **git's own diagnostics are pinned to English** (`LC_ALL=C`). The plugin's text is still localised by the setting; git's is kept stable because the phrase table in `lib/text.js` matches English sentences, and a localised git defeats it — worse on Windows, where git writes in the console code page and the pipeline decodes UTF-8, so a Chinese message arrives as mojibake.
- **The

plugins.description: Side-by-side session grid for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI: click sessions in the sidebar, get an equal-cell grid of live conversations (max 3 per row), drag the top-right handle to reorder, each pane keeps its own composer.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-multi-chat

**Side-by-side sessions for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI, as an equal-cell grid.**
Click a session in the left sidebar and it joins the conversation area as its own pane: one
click → one session, three clicks → three sessions. At most **three panes per row**; the grid
degrades to two or one column when the window is narrow. The session you clicked (the shell's
current session) stays highlighted, every pane keeps its own bottom-pinned input box, and panes
can be reordered by dragging the **⠿ handle in the top-right corner** of a pane header.

中文说明：[README.zh.md](README.zh.md) · 设计依据：[docs/design.md](docs/design.md) ·
Design notes (EN): [docs/design.en.md](docs/design.en.md)

---

## What it does

| | |
|---|---|
| **Follow the sidebar** | Every session you click in the sidebar becomes a pane. The pane order survives a page reload. |
| **Equal-cell grid** | At most three equal cells per row (`3 × 3` = 9 panes max, six by default). Rows share the height but never below a comfortable pane height (~420 px); beyond that the grid scrolls. Narrow windows degrade 3 → 2 → 1 columns. |
| **Highlight** | The current session's pane is ringed, its title emphasized, and its sequence badge inverts. |
| **Focus by click** | Clicking inside a non-active pane asks the shell to make that session current (the official sidebar highlight follows). |
| **Reorder by drag** | Grab the ⠿ handle at the top-right of a pane header (immediate drag) or press the header itself (4 px of travel, or a 300 ms hold on touch). Drop on another pane to **swap** the two, drop on empty grid space to move the pane to the end, `Esc` cancels. The dragged pane follows the pointer as a ghost card and the drop target is outlined. |
| **Reorder by keyboard** | The handle is focusable: `Ctrl/⌘ + arrows` swaps with the neighbouring cell (grid-aware for up/down), otherwise nothing happens. |
| **Close** | Each pane has a close control. The active pane can only be closed by handing the shell over to a sibling — otherwise the control is disabled with a reason. The toolbar's **Keep only active** collapses the grid. |
| **Sidebar toggle** | Each session row gets an extra action button (next to archive/pin) that adds/removes that session as a pane **without** navigating. |
| **Degrade, never break** | A single pane → the official single-session UI is used untouched. Unknown/closed sessions render a note card. A crashed pane is contained by a pane-level error boundary. No `slots`/`sessions` service → the plugin stays inert instead of failing the web boot. |

## Install

The package is a DSH bundle plugin: the host half (`.` → `lib/index.js`) only exists so the
package becomes a loader entry; the browser half (`./client` → `lib/client.js`) is what the web
shell loads through the `dsh.client` declaration.

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<path-to-this-package>
# then restart the desktop app / profile (bundle layers apply at boot)
```

Read-only check that the row composes (writes nothing):

```powershell
dsh --profile desktop --dump-config | Select-String dsh-multi-chat
```

Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-multi-chat`.

## Development

```powershell
npm install    # dev-only: react, react-dom, jsdom, yaml, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots
npm test       # 7 suites, 90 tests
npm run typecheck
```

**v0.3.0 feature — the grid can be switched off**: pick **Settings → Plugins → dsh-multi-chat** and flip
*Enable the side-by-side grid* (or press **Exit grid** in the grid toolbar). Off returns the conversation area to
the official single-session view; the panes you had opened are remembered, so switching back on brings the grid
straight back. The preference is stored separately from the pane order, so toggling can never disturb it.

**v0.2.6 fix**: the official turn navigator (the tick rail with turn previews on the right of a
conversation) hid itself inside every pane, because the official stylesheet hides it whenever its
conversation container is narrower than 900px. One pane-scoped rule with higher specificity restores it
(the official class prefix is read from the official stylesheet at runtime, and nothing is injected when
that stylesheet is missing). Verified live: the rail renders 28×102px with its marks inside a 456px pane.

**v0.2.5 fix**: the column count was hard-coded to three, so two sessions left a third of the row empty.
The grid now fills: columns follow the available width (`auto-fit` collapses the tracks no pane lands in),
two panes share the row, and three across appears only when the width allows — panes stay at least ~400px
wide. Measured at a 1680px window: two panes = 2×688px (100% of the row), three = 3×456px, four = 3+1
equal cells.

**v0.2.4 change**: the grid is a wide-window feature, so a narrow window keeps the official single
session view. Below 720px of window width the plugin is completely inert — no session is retained, no
slot is replaced, and nothing is written to the shared storage (which the floating session window would
otherwise clobber with its own pane set). Widening the window brings the grid back; narrowing hands the
conversation area back. Verified live: 490×640 cold start shows the normal conversation, 1680×1050 shows
the grid, resizing switches both ways.

**v0.2.3 fix**: in a narrow window (the ~490 px floating session window) the grid toolbar wrapped into
three lines and squeezed the conversation. It now never wraps and degrades by width — dropping the drag
hint, then the usage counter, swapping the title for a compact "N panes" label — and the row height
yields to short windows (`min(420px, 62vh)`). Measured in a 490×640 window: one 37 px line, single
column, composer fully visible.

**v0.2.2 fixes** (reported from a live session, located in a real browser): the grid used to be
registered in a *session-scoped* slot, which the renderer remounts whenever the shell switches
session — so every switch rebuilt the grid and all pane conversations (the lag that grew with the
number of panes) and replaced the composer input mid-click (the "needs a second click to focus"
bug). The grid now lives in the **root-scope `main` / `conversation` panel cell** (same replacement
semantics, no remount), and pane activation runs on `focusin`/`click` instead of `pointerdown`.
Measured live: one click focuses the composer, session switching ≈ one frame, 5 panes ≈ 2.6k DOM
nodes with off-screen panes virtualised. Details: [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) §4.9.

**v0.2.1 fixes**: switching a session no longer walks a `retain` → publish → `retain` recursion (it
used to overflow the stack, slow every switch down and leave the pane ring and the sidebar highlight
disagreeing); dragging can no longer strand a ghost or a drop ring when the pointer is released
outside the grid; the selection ring is a single crisp outer ring instead of a double-drawn edge.
Details and the reproduction evidence: [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) §4.8.

| Suite | Covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/manifest.test.mjs` | package/bundle/client-half/patch/locale contract, plus "the composer fix stays in place" |
| `tests/host.test.mjs` | the inert host half never throws |
| `tests/store.test.mjs` | pane ledger: follow adds panes, ceiling 6/9, eviction, highlight, `swap`/`moveToEnd`, persistence + the v1→v2 migration, untrusted payloads, drop targeting, keyboard steps |
| `tests/registration.test.mjs` | activation contract: no registration for one pane, shadow registration for 2+, retention/release, sidebar button, unknown sessions, disposal, missing services |
| `tests/real-slot-core.test.mjs` | the same wiring driven through the **real** `SlotCore` shipped by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots` |
| `tests/render.test.mjs` | structural rendering: equal-cell grid, single highlight, handle + close per header, `variant: 'embedded'` for the conversation body, hero/settling phases, token-only stylesheet |
| `tests/interaction.test.mjs` | React DOM in jsdom: pointer drag → swap, drop on empty → move to end, `Esc` cancel, header 4 px threshold, `Ctrl+Arrow` keyboard swap, close/focus, sidebar toggle, toolbar, pane-level crash containment |

End-to-end install verificati

plugins.description: A Restart button for DeepSeek Harness Settings: replaces the dsh web process serving the page, then reconnects the page by itself.
plugins.readme_text: **A Restart card in DeepSeek Harness Settings.** One click replaces the `dsh web` process that is serving your page — and the page reconnects by itself. No terminal, no re-opening the desktop icon. That matters because some changes cannot hot-reload: - you changed a plugin's **host half**, and Node caches imported ES modules by URL; - you edited `config.json`, the port, or the workspace; - a session holds in-memory state you want gone. Today those mean walking back to a terminal. This plugin turns them into one click. ## Try it ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:chenkui-luo/dsh-plugin-restart ``` Then **refresh the page once** and open **Settings → Restart**. Without the `dsh` CLI (no pnpm, or a patched profile): copy the package into `/node_modules/dsh-plugin-restart` and add this row to `/cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - insert: - id: restart name: 'dsh-plugin-restart' ``` The bundled installer does both steps with a backup and a read-back check before it writes: ```powershell powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\Install-RestartPlugin.ps1 powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\Install-RestartPlugin.ps1 -Action disable powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\Install-RestartPlugin.ps1 -Action uninstall ``` ## What happens when you click | Step | What runs | | --- | --- | | 1 | The page sends `POST /dsh-restart/restart` — same origin, authenticated | | 2 | The host half starts a **detached helper** and answers the request *before* anything is stopped | | 3 | The helper waits for the port to stop accepting connections, then hands over to your launcher | | 4 | The launcher starts a fresh `dsh web` with a new launch token and writes its token file | | 5 | The helper confirms the replacement is up, then lets the old process exit — gracefully | | 6 | The page sees a new instance id on its next poll and reloads itself | Nothing is force-killed in the middle of the response, and the old process is stopped **last**, by itself. A restart that fails leaves a diagnosis in the log instead of failing silently. ## Why the helper is a detached **node** process This part was measured on a real Windows machine, not assumed: | how a background helper is started | does it run | does it outlive the process it must replace | | --- | --- | --- | | PowerShell, `detached: true` | **no** — exits 0, silently | — | | PowerShell, attached | yes | no — dies with its parent | | **node, `detached: true`** | yes | **yes** | | node, attached | yes | no | On Windows a "detached" PowerShell child gets no console and never runs the script — the same trap [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) documents. An attached helper dies together with the process it is supposed to replace. So the helper is a detached node process, and it gives its own children a hidden console through `powershell -WindowStyle Hidden`. Force-killing the whole tree is the other half of the story: it leaves a Windows port unbindable long enough for the replacement to die with `EADDRINUSE`. Waiting for the port to go quiet and only then starting the replacement is what makes the handover reliable. ## Verified, not asserted | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Helper generation, offline (`runtime-test/CheckHelperScript.mjs`) | 11/11 | | End to end, real plugin code (`runtime-test/VerifyRestartPlugin.mjs`) | 21/21 | | **Real** launcher + **real** `dsh web`, full restart cycle (`runtime-test/SmokeRestartReal.ps1`) | pass | The end-to-end runs cover: the installer writing a managed patch row, the host half claiming its routes, an unauthenticated request being fenced off, the restart being accepted before the port goes away, a second click inside the guard window being refused, the port wait, the launcher handover, the successor process appearing, and the page noticing it. These live in the toolkit this plugin was built in; this repository is the packaged plugin. ## API Every route passes the connection trust fence (loopback peer + matching `Origin` + login cookie), so only an authenticated same-origin page can reach them. | Method | Path | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | GET | `/dsh-restart/status` | `instanceId` (this server's pid), port, workspace, launcher path and availability, whether a restart is in flight | | POST | `/dsh-restart/restart` | Arms a restart. A second request within 15 s gets `409`. The response carries **no** launch token | | GET | `/dsh-restart/log` | Tail of the shared restart log | If the automatic reload comes back unauthenticated — a fresh launch token is minted on every start — the page's own token is handed back to the *same* browser connection once, so it can reopen itself with `?token=…`. ## Logs `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepSeekHarness\restart-plugin\logs\restart.log` — append-only, so the record of a restart survives the process that performed it. The helper writes the launcher's exit code, whether the port is still being served, and whether a fresh token file appeared, because the process that would normally log a failure is the one that just exited. ## Configuration | Variable | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `DSH_RESTART_INSTALL_DIR` | Launcher runtime directory (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepSeekHarness`) | | `DSH_RESTART_DATA` | Plugin-private data directory (default `\restart-plugin`) | | `DSH_RESTART_LAUNCHER` | Point at another launcher script (portable installs, tests) | **Restart target.** By default it delegates to the launcher a hosted install already has (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepSeekHarness\Launch-DeepSeekHarness.ps1`), which owns the reliable stop/start/readiness sequence. When that file is missing the button reports a clear error instead of pretending to work, and the status card shows the path it looked for. Making the plugin fully standalone is the next step on the roadmap. ## Safety - Authenticated same-origin loopback only; proxy-forwarded requests are not honoured. - No admin rights, no system configuration touched. - It **interrupts a running conversation turn** — that is what a restart is, and the card says so. - If the port is owned by a process the launcher does not recognise (a `dsh web` you started by hand), the restart takes that port over, including its terminal's process tree. ## Credits - **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)** — the open-source agent harness this plugin extends and is built on: its `dsh.bundle` + `cordis.patch.yml` declaration, the dual host/browser plugin shape, and the webserver's trust fence. [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) · MIT. - **[dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market)** — the community plugin market. Its `restart.js` is the reference for the approach used here: delegate to a detached helper, wait for the port instead of guessing with a fixed delay, and make a failed restart leave evidence. ## License MIT

plugins.description: A transparent always-on-top desktop pet for DSH on Linux (X11 / XWayland)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-pet-desktop-linux

[**English**](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A desktop pet for DSH (DeepSeek Harness) on Linux: a small transparent,
always-on-top GTK3 window that floats over your desktop and animates according to
what your DSH sessions are doing — idle, working, waiting for an answer, failed,
or finished and awaiting review. It is not click-through: the window keeps its
input region, so clicks on the pet land on the pet.

**Platform: Linux with X11 or XWayland only.** Windows, macOS and native Wayland
(no XWayland) are not supported. See [Requirements](#requirements).

![The pet floating transparently over the desktop](assets/screenshots/desktop-pet-linux-1.png)

The window has no background and no border — the wallpaper shows through, and the
pet stays on top of ordinary windows. The sprite follows your DSH sessions:

![Idle, working, waiting, failed and review poses](assets/screenshots/desktop-pet-linux-2.png)

> **Canonical copy:** this plugin is only published as
> `dsh-pet-desktop-linux` (no scope) under the `Wlaeg` account. Any other
> package with this name is not ours.

---

## This is not a meta-package

This plugin ships **its own working program**; it is not a bundle that only
re-exports somebody else's dependency list:

| Part | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop program | `desktop/pet.py` | The pet window itself: GTK3 transparent window, spritesheet animation, right-click menu, work-status dialog |
| Host half | `lib/index.js` | Probes system dependencies, spawns/stops the Python program, exposes the HTTP routes, reads and writes the config file |
| Browser half | `client.js` | The **Desktop Pet** panel in DSH Settings, with the packaged `locale/{en,zh}.json` manifest strings |

The single dependency, `@michengai/dsh-codex-pet`, is used **only to read the pet
sprite sheets**. This plugin deliberately does not copy that artwork into its own
repository: store rules require a bundle's dependencies to resolve to the original
author's published package, so this plugin depends on the upstream npm package
and resolves the artwork path at runtime
(`require.resolve('@michengai/dsh-codex-pet/package.json')`). See
[Artwork and licensing](#artwork-and-licensing).

The upstream plugin draws a pet **inside the DSH web page**. This plugin draws a
**separate always-on-top desktop window** that works while the page is in the
background, minimized, or closed. They are different things, not duplicates.

---

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Platform | **Linux with X11 or XWayland.** Verified on Manjaro GNOME (Wayland session, pet runs through XWayland) |
| DSH | Any DSH build with the Cordis plugin system that provides `webServer` and the `settings.section` slot |
| Node | **>= 22** (DSH's own requirement) |
| Desktop session | A GTK3-capable session. Under GNOME/Wayland the pet is an XWayland client — a **pure Wayland session with XWayland disabled will not work** |
| npm dependencies | `@michengai/dsh-codex-pet` (artwork lookup only) |

### System packages

The Settings panel probes five of these — Python 3, PyGObject, GTK3, GdkPixbuf
and `xdotool` — and shows the matching install hint for your distribution when
one is missing. The other two rows (the WebP loader and `zstd`) are not probed;
check them yourself with the commands below if the pet starts but looks wrong.

| Component | Arch / Manjaro | Debian / Ubuntu | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python 3 | `python` | `python3` | `python3` |
| Python 3 + PyGObject (`import gi`) | `python-gobject` | `python3-gi` | `python3-gobject` |
| GTK3 typelib | `gtk3` | `gir1.2-gtk-3.0` | `gtk3` |
| GdkPixbuf typelib | `gdk-pixbuf2` | `gir1.2-gdkpixbuf-2.0` | `gdk-pixbuf2` |
| WebP loader for GdkPixbuf | *(built into `gdk-pixbuf2`)* | `webp-pixbuf-loader` | `webp-pixbuf-loader` |
| `zstd` CLI *(only if Python < 3.14)* | `zstd` | `zstd` | `zstd` |
| xdotool | `xdotool` | `xdotool` | `xdotool` |

```sh
# Arch / Manjaro
sudo pacman -S python python-gobject gtk3 gdk-pixbuf2 zstd xdotool

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install python3 python3-gi gir1.2-gtk-3.0 gir1.2-gdkpixbuf-2.0 webp-pixbuf-loader zstd xdotool

# Fedora
sudo dnf install python3 python3-gobject gtk3 gdk-pixbuf2 webp-pixbuf-loader zstd xdotool
```

The session event files are zstd-compressed. Python 3.14 and newer decode them
with the standard library (`compression.zstd`); on older interpreters the plugin
falls back to the `zstd` command-line tool, so install `zstd` if your `python3`
is older than 3.14. Without either, the pet still runs but never leaves `idle`.

The sprite sheets are WebP files, so GdkPixbuf must be able to decode WebP.
Depending on your distribution's GdkPixbuf version this may need the separate
`webp-pixbuf-loader` package (Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora). You can check yours with
the command below; if it prints `False`, install the loader package:

```sh
python3 -c "import gi; gi.require_version('GdkPixbuf','2.0'); \
from gi.repository import GdkPixbuf; \
print('webp' in [f.get_name() for f in GdkPixbuf.Pixbuf.get_formats()])"
```

The plugin's dependency probe checks GTK3, GdkPixbuf and `xdotool` by name but
does not decode a WebP sprite itself; if the loader is missing, the pet window
appears and the sprite fails to load, which shows up in the log tail.

`xdotool` is used for the two EWMH window hints GTK3 cannot set by itself:
`_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE` (keep above) and `_NET_WM_STATE_STICKY` (show on every
workspace). Without it the pet still appears, but it will not stay on top of
other windows or follow you across workspaces.

Decoding goes through `GdkPixbuf.PixbufLoader` and frames are drawn as
`Gtk.Image` pixbufs, so **Pillow is not needed**, and because no drawing goes
through a `cairo.Context`, **pycairo is not needed either**.

---

## Installation

This is a DSH Cordis plugin **bundle**. Install it through DSH's plugin manager
(`plugin_manager`, action `install_bundle`), pointing `target` at either:

- the **Git repository** — `https://github.com/Wlaeg/dsh-pet-desktop-linux`
- or a **local checkout** — the absolute path to this directory

Equivalently, from a DSH shell:

```sh
# once published to npm
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-pet-desktop-linux

# straight from the repository
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wlaeg/dsh-pet-desktop-linux

# from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-pet-desktop-linux
```

The bundle declares its own patch in `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dsh": {
    "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" },
    "client": {
      "platform": "web",
      "immediately": true,
      "inject": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer"]
    }
  },
  "icon": "./assets/icon.png"
}
```

(`dsh.client.inject` is a client-module **load-order** declaration: DSH loads the
listed packages' browser bundles before this one. It is not Cordis service
injection. The browser half declares the services it actually needs itself:
`return { inject: ['slots', 'locale'], apply }`.)

and that patch is a single `insert` that mounts the host half:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-pet-desktop-linux
      name: 'dsh-pet-desktop-linux'
      config: {}
```

The browser half is declared by `dsh.client` and bound to the row whose `name` is
the bare package name — subpath rows do not carry a browser half.

After installing, reload the DSH Web UI page so the browser half registers its
Settings panel. Nothing else is required: **DSH starts the pet window by itself**
as soon as it boots (`autostart` defaults to `true` — see “Configuration”). The
pet process stops when you stop it or uninstall the bundle.

> Replacing an already-installed copy (for example after editing the source)
> needs a restart of the DSH host process — the running process keeps the JS
> module generation it loaded at startup. A page reload is not enough.

---

## Features

**Window**

- Borderless, transparent GTK3 window — only the pet is visible, the window
  background is fully transparent
- Always on top (`_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE`), so it stays above normal windows
- Sticky across workspaces (`_NET_WM_STATE_STICKY`, via `xdotool`) — no API for
  this exists in GT

plugins.description: DSH 助手人格与长期记忆插件：独立可用，不依赖其它插件。管 AI 自身的名字与角色、对用户的称呼、回复风格与自定义指令；人设支持全局 + 按工作区两级覆盖；长期记忆走三段式（候选捕获 → 待审缓冲区 → 用户裁决才生效），并支持一键导入其它 AI 的历史记忆。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-anima

DSH 的**助手人格与外挂记忆层**——一个独立插件，装上即可用。

它管的是「**你自己（助手）是谁**」：AI 的名字与角色、你对它的称呼、回复风格、
以及你自己写的行为准则；再加一套**带待审缓冲区的长期记忆**，
以及输入框光轨、输入框快捷开关、工具确认门槛这些界面能力。
字段集不依赖任何其它插件，也不从别处读取配置。

> **工具名为什么是 `set_assistant_persona`**：`tools.register()` 遇同层重名直接抛错
> （`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:2634`），与生态里任何同名工具共存时必有一方注册失败、
> 被 `.catch` 吞成一行 warn —— 那是发布级的静默故障。功能相似不要求撞名。

---

## 它解决什么

| 能力 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **AI 自己的名字与角色** | `agentName` / `agentRole` —— 决定它怎么称呼自己、以什么身份说话 |
| 用户的称呼 / 背景 / 语气 / 长度 / 语言 | `addressUserAs` / `userOccupation` / `userBio` / `style` / `replyLength` / `language` |
| **按工作区两层覆盖** | 只覆盖声明的字段，其余继承全局；覆盖文件随目录走、可 git |
| **长期记忆** | 自动沉淀 → 待审缓冲区 → 用户裁决 → 注入 |
| 输入框光轨 / 快捷开关 / 工具确认 | 界面与安全开关 |
| 人设预设 | 6 条内置 + 自建；也可把当前配置存成预设 |
| **十二个字段全是自由文本** | 存的就是注入的原话，另有「一键填入 + 示例」按钮组 |
| **记忆随工作区分层** | 全局记忆处处生效，工作区记忆只在匹配时注入 |
| **注入可解释 / 字符预算** | 每条为什么进 / 不进，条数与字符双约束 |
| **本地聚类与冲突提示** | 纯本地 bigram 相似度，只提示不自动合并 |
| **人设变更审计日志** | 谁在什么时候把哪个字段改成什么 |
| **一键导入外部 AI 的记忆** | 复制提示词 → 粘贴结果 → 机械切分 → 逐条裁决层级 |
| 长期记忆的「自动写入」 | ❌ 刻意不做（见下） |

### 关于与 `dsh-soul` 的关系

上表左侧的能力划分与 `dsh-soul` 0.7.0 的字段集**有交集**，实现上也刻意与它保持一致
（工具确认语义、光轨动效参数、重置保留预设）。但本插件**不依赖它**：
字段集完整自持，不读它的配置文件，两者可同时安装且标识全部错开。
这层关系的完整说明见下方「[致谢与差异化声明](#致谢与差异化声明)」。

## 四个差异化设计

功能对齐不等于没有自己的判断。以下四点是本插件相对主流记忆插件的**真实增量**，
每一条都对应一个具体的失败模式。

### 1. 双约束注入：条数与字符同时生效

多数实现只有一个「最多注入 N 条」的上限。问题是 40 条长记忆一样能挤爆上下文，
而用户看到的是「我只设了 40 条啊」。

本插件的 `selectForInjection` 同时受 `memory.maxInjected`（条数，默认 40）与
`memory.maxInjectedChars`（字符，默认 4000）约束，**取先到者**。两条上限各有各的适用场景：
条数管「别让模型看太多碎片」，字符管「别让一次注入吃掉半屏上下文」。

### 2. 注入可解释：看得见每条为什么进 / 不进

注入不是黑箱。设置页的「注入情况」列出**每一条已采纳记忆**的去留与原因：

| 原因码 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `included` | 已注入提示词 |
| `other-workspace` | 属于别的工作区，不在本会话注入 |
| `no-workspace-context` | 当前会话没有工作区信息，无法匹配工作区记忆 |
| `workspace-scope-unknown` | 标记为工作区记忆但没记录属于哪个工作区 |
| `over-max` | 已采纳条数超过注入上限，按时间取最新的 |
| `over-budget` | 单条就超出字符预算，取不下 |
| `dropped-by-budget` | 前面几条已占满字符预算 |
| `no-injection` | 记忆层已关闭或上限为 0 |

区分 `over-budget` 与 `dropped-by-budget` 是刻意的：前者要删那条，后者要腾位置 ——
报同一个码，用户不知道该动谁。原因文案由宿主下发（`INJECTION_REASON_TEXT` 只有一份），
客户端不重写翻译。

### 3. 本地聚类：只提示，不自动合并

待审缓冲区里若有多条明显在说同一件事，插件用**字符二元组（bigram）的 Jaccard 系数**
（纯本地、零依赖、零模型调用）算出相似度，把「这 3 条像在说同一件事」摆到用户面前。

**刻意不做自动合并**：合并意味着生成一段用户没说过的话。本插件的立场是
「判断什么值得记交给模型，什么真的生效交给用户」——自动合并恰好违背它。
聚类只让裁决更快，不替他裁决。同理「候选撞上已采纳记忆」只提示冲突，不改任何数据。

### 4. 人设变更审计日志

本插件有三个入口能改人设：设置页、`/anima` 命令、模型调用的 `set_assistant_persona` 工具。
而「工具确认」**默认是关的** —— 也就是说，模型可以直接把你叫它什么、它用什么语气回话改掉，
而你无从知道是谁在什么时候干的。

审计日志只记「改了什么」，不做判断、不参与提示词。它挂在 `StateStore.updateConfig` 这**一个**
收口上，而不是在各调用点分别埋点：所有写入路径最终都走这里，分散埋点迟早会漏掉一条，
而漏掉的那条恰恰可能是模型的静默改写。`resetConfig` 也走审计 —— 否则
「昨天还好好的，今天全空了」在日志里查无此事。

记录上限 200 条，独立成表（不塞进 `config`）：`config` 每次启动整条读入内存，
审计会涨到几百条，混在一起等于让启动开销随使用时长上升。
长值在写入时截断为 200 字并附「共 N 字」，数组/对象只记规模 —— 审计是索引，不是备份。

看到它的地方有两处：设置页「变更记录」卡（完整列表，可按条清空），
以及 `/anima show` 的**「最近变更」一行**——只显示最新那条，格式是
`[MM-DD HH:mm] <来源>：<字段名>`，**刻意不带具体值**：值可能很私人，而 `show`
的输出会被复制到对话里问人。

## 致谢与差异化声明

本插件的功能集**参考**了 [dsh-soul](https://github.com/Aliuyanfeng/dsh-soul)（MIT）与
`dsh-checkpoint-rewind` 的设计，并在若干处刻意与它们保持行为一致（存储惰性解析、
失败关闭的确认语义、重置保留用户预设、光轨动效参数）。

需要明确的是：

- **代码全部独立实现**，未拷贝上述项目的源码、注释、提示词文案或图形资源。
- 两处**动效参数刻意取同值**（8 层错位描边、虚线段长 12 / 步进 2.2 / 圆角 22 等），
  理由是避免同一台机器上出现两套观感。这类数值属于思想与参数，不受著作权保护；
  记在这里是为了不让读者误以为拷贝。
- **导航图标刻意画得不同形**：dsh-soul 用「光轨弧 + 火花」，本插件用「人像（头+肩）+ 火花」，
  单色 `currentColor`，viewBox 也另行收紧。
- **各类标识全部错开**，避免共存时互相顶替或注册失败：

  | 类别 | dsh-soul | 本插件 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 工具名 | `set_persona` | `set_assistant_persona` |
  | 设置页 id | `soul-settings` | `anima-settings` |
  | 光轨槽位 id | `soul-trail` | `anima-trail` |
  | 开关槽位 id | `soul-quick-toggle` | `anima-quick-toggle` |
  | 提示词 section | `soul:persona` | `anima:identity` / `:memory` / `:pending` |
  | 存储域 | —（自有文件） | `anima` |
  | 注入来源 kind | `plugin:dsh-soul` | `plugin:dsh-anima` |

工具名错开不只是礼貌：`dsh-tools` 的 `register()` 遇同层重名**直接抛错**
（`lib/index.js` 的 `NamedEntries` 冲突工厂），两者共存时必有一方注册失败、
并被 `.catch` 吞成一行 warn —— 那是发布级的静默故障。



## 核心设计：三段式记忆

这是本插件与市面上 15+ 记忆插件最不一样的地方。

```
对话中通过 remember 工具投递
        ↓
   待审缓冲区（不生效）
        ↓  每晚自动整理：去重 / 淘汰 / 与已采纳项比对
        ↓
   通知用户「有 N 条待你裁决」
        ↓
   用户在设置页逐个「采纳 / 丢弃 / 删除」
        ↓
   已采纳 → 注入提示词
```

**为什么不做静默自动写入**：记忆一旦静默写入就直接影响后续所有回答，写错了用户很难发现。
本插件把「判断什么值得记」交给模型，把「什么真的生效」交给用户。

整理这一步**纯本地、不调用模型**——只做去重、淘汰、与已采纳项比对，不做语义归纳。

记忆**分两层**：`global` 处处生效，`workspace` 只在 `cwd` 归一化后完全相等时注入。
不做「子目录继承」——工作区覆盖是精确匹配语义，记忆若采用继承语义，
用户在子目录里会看到父目录的记忆，排查起来极难。
分层之外的注入解释、预算与聚类见上文「四个差异化设计」。

## 凭据闸门

任何命中凭据形态的内容**在进入缓冲区之前就被拒收**（不落盘、不留痕），
覆盖私钥块、OpenAI/AWS/GitHub 令牌、通用 api_key / secret / 密码赋值、Bearer、
URL 内嵌凭据等 11 类模式。

理由：内容一旦落盘缓冲区，就处于「等待进入提示词」的状态，凭据不该走这条路。
凭据判定用的是 11 类正则的机械匹配，没有语义理解，会有误判——所以被拦下时界面会
把命中规则名一起说出来，用户可以删掉那串字符再粘贴。

## 一键导入外部 AI 的记忆

设置页记忆卡里有一个「导入外部 AI 的记忆」按钮，展开后是两步：

1. **复制提示词**——把一段整理画像的提示词发给你用得最多的那个 AI，让它把你的偏好
   整理成清单。按钮只在真的写进剪贴板后才显示「已复制」；没有剪贴板 API 时会明说
   「复制失败，请手动选中后复制」，不假装成功。
2. **粘贴结果**——粘贴框接受 AI 的输出，也接受你自己手写的笔记（不要求必须是 AI 生成的）。

解析后逐条预览，每条都能改层级（全局 / 本工作区）或直接丢弃，确认后才写进**待审缓冲区**
——和手动添加、模型投递走同一条路，仍然要用户逐条裁决才生效。

**切分是机械的，不做语义理解**：按 Markdown 标题、列表项、空行三种边界切；刻意不按句号切，
因为中文画像里「偏好：结论先行。」被切成两条会读不通。小节标签（如「我的使用画像」）
不进候选——它长得像记忆但没有可采纳内容。

**归类是建议不是判决**：`suggestLayer` 只看措辞——提到具体磁盘路径或「本项目 / 这个项目」
建议 `workspace`，提到「所有项目 / 一律 / 每次都要」建议 `global`。两条都没有时默认 `global`，
理由是把「记忆动不动就不生效」当默认体验，比跨项目污染更糟。每条建议都带一句理由显示在
条目下方，用户看到「本工作区」就能立刻知道凭什么。

**解析阶段就分流**：一条原文切完后按顺序过五道闸，没通过的会被分别归到不同的桶里，
每一桶都在界面上显示出来，**不静默少一条**：

| 处置 | 判定 | 界面上 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 过短（`< 4` 信息量） | 切出的碎片太短，通常是编号残留 | 只在汇总里报个数 |
| 超长（`> 500` 字） | 单条超过记忆上限 | 不截断，明确告知「请拆成几条」 |
| 凭据 | 命中 11 类正则之一 | 整条拦下并说明命中了哪条规则 |
| 重复 | 与已有记忆文本相同 | 单独列出 |
| 超条数 | 超出单次上限（默认 60 条） | 余下部分不进这一批，另开一次导入 |
| 同义 | 与待审缓冲区里的某条相似度 ≥ 0.6 | 在条目下方提示「已有一条很像」，**不自动合并** |

原文上限 40000 字符，超出直接报错而不是截断（截断等于偷偷丢掉用户画像的后半段）。
同义提示刻意只提示不合并：自动合并会生成一段用户从没说过的话。

---

## 安装

### 从 GitHub 安装（推荐）

本插件尚未发布到 npm，从仓库直接装：

```
dsh plugin add github:Melody-cx/dsh-anima#v1.0.0
```

或者手工改 profile 的 `package.json`：

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-anima": "github:Melody-cx/dsh-anima#v1.0.0"
  },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ /* ... */ "dsh-anima" ] } }
}
```

`#v1.0.0` 是标签（也可以写 commit SHA，或整个省略以跟随 `main`）。**建议 pin 住一个版本**，
否则上游的任何改动都会在下次安装时直接进入你的 profile。git 源下载的是**整个仓库 tarball**
（本仓库很小），首次安装可能比 npm 源慢一些，超时的话重试一次即可。

然后 `pnpm install`，**重启 DSH**。宿主侧改动一律需要重启才生效。

### 从源码安装（开发用）

在 profile 的 `package.json` 里加依赖（也可以用 `/plugins` 界面）：

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-anima": "file:<仓库目录的绝对路径>"
  },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ /* ... */ "dsh-anima" ] } }
}
```

本地 `file:` 依赖是**复制**语义：改完源码要**重新安装**才生效，且重跑安装时若 pnpm 判定
`changed:false` 会直接跳过 —— 正确姿势是先 `remove_bundle` 再 `install_bundle`
（或比对 `node_modules` 副本与源码的 SHA256）。

**运行前提**（`package.json` 里已声明，装不上时先看这几条）：

- `engines.node` = `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`，`engines.dsh` = `>=0.1.6-0 <0.2.0 || >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0`
- `peerDependencies` 四包：`@deepseek-ai/cordis`（`^4.0.1 || ^4.0.5-alpha.1`）、
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`
  —— 它们由宿主提供，插件不打包它们
- `dependencies.zod`（`^4.4.3`）是唯一真正要装的运行时依赖
- 存储栈需在 profile 里组合：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage` + `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json`（配 `root`）
  + `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain`（配 `backend: json`）。缺了不会崩，但插件会退化成
  「存储不可用」，设置页会明说原因（见下「存储」一节）

## 配置

设置页新增一栏「**灵台**」（`settings.section` id = `anima-settings`，order 51）。

- **助手身份**：`enabled` / `agentName` / `agentRole` / `addressUserAs` / `userOccupation` / `userBio`
- **回复风格**：`style` / `headingLists` / `emoji` / `tables` / `replyLength` / `language` / `customInstructions`
- **工作区覆盖**：`workspaceOverridesEnabled` / `workspaceFileDir`
  覆盖文件默认写在 `<工作区>/.dsh-anima/override.json`（目录名可用 `workspaceFileDir` 改），随目录走、可 git、可拷给别人；
  该目录会自动写入 `.gitignore`（内容 `*`），避免私人语气设定被推到远程。
- **输入框光轨**：`trailEnabled` / `trailColor`（`#RRGGBB`，落盘统一大写）/ `trailSpeed`（`slow|normal|fast`）/ `trailWidth`（`thin|normal|thick`）
- **工具确认**：`requireToolConfirmation` —— 开启后模型调 `set_assistant_persona` 只**提交提议**，不写配置
- **长期记忆**：`memory.enabled` / `autoCapture` / `nightlyTriage` / `nightlyHour` / `maxPending` /
  `maxInjected` / `maxInjectedChars` / `notifyOnSessionStart` / `defaultLayer`

### 不做任何迁移

本插件**不读任何其它插件或自己旧版本的配置**。它是 1.0.0，此前没有发布过任何版本 ——
没有「老用户的介质」这种东西需要兼容，所以代码里既没有一次性迁移，也没有存储格式回退。
这两块曾存在于开发期，都已删除；留着它们的唯一作用是让后人以为有一批需要照顾的存

plugins.description: 给 DSH 里助手回复加气泡底，可选液态玻璃材质；工具条、过程行、统计行等周边信息也能一起同步
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-assistant-bubble [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) 使用皮肤插件从wallpaper里导入深色壁纸时，会发现ai回复的文字是无背景的，导致字和壁纸糊在一起无法阅读。所以让大肥鱼单独写了一个小插件实现气泡功能。 这下可以愉快地使用壁纸了。 . 有一些气泡间距的小问题，可能对观感有小影响，但是不太好修，所以就放在那里了， 插件开启前 开启后。气泡透明度之类的可以自己调，单独在设置里开了“助手回复气泡”的分区页。 ————以下内容都是肥鱼写的 给 DSH 里**助手回复**加一层自己的气泡底，可选液态玻璃材质；工具条、过程行、统计行等周边信息也能一起同步。 ## 为什么需要它 DSH 官方会话界面里，气泡（`..._bubble`）只属于**你发送的消息**；助手回复是一段**没有背景**的正文， 直接压在壁纸上。所以壁纸 / 皮肤类插件的"气泡不透明度""玻璃透明度"都管不到助手回复 —— 深色壁纸下助手的字就看不清了。这个插件补的就是这一块。 ## 功能 - **助手回复气泡**：圆角 + 可调底色；可选液态玻璃（白釉高光 + 模糊 + 厚玻璃折射 + 落地阴影）。 - **周边信息同步**：工具条（复制 / 点赞 / 分享 / 用量 / 时间）、过程折叠行、过程分组头（运行中）、 思考触发条、会话统计行、上下文占用环、运行行 —— 同一份材质、同一组参数，滑块一动一起变。 - **只给"真的有内容"的元素画底**：每个锚点都先核对有没有看得见的文字（≥2 个字）或可见的按钮 / 图标， 空壳一律不画 —— 所以不会出现"只有底色、没有文字"的空白气泡。 - **「工作步骤展示」明细行**：工具调用行（「运行命令」「网页获取」等）与「思考」行也有气泡 —— **折叠**时是紧凑小胶囊、**展开**时保持宿主原本的大横条。 - **操作条常驻**：取消宿主"非最后一条要悬停才显示"的门控。 - **宽度跟随内容**：气泡不拉满整行。 - **宽表格收进气泡**：宿主原本让宽表格按滚动容器整屏出血，这里改为气泡内横向滚动。 - **无障碍**：系统开启「减少透明度」时自动去掉模糊与白釉。 ## 安装 ```bash # 从 GitHub 安装（最新 main） dsh plugin --profile web add github:yutianliang/dsh-assistant-bubble ``` 官方桌面端也可以走侧边栏 **插件** 页 → 添加插件 → 填 `github:yutianliang/dsh-assistant-bubble`。 本地改代码时用 `link:`：`dsh plugin --profile web add link:E:\path\to\dsh-assistant-bubble`。 卸载：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-assistant-bubble`。 ## 设置 安装后，**设置 →「助手回复气泡」**（独立分区，10 个控件）： | 控件 | 作用 | 默认 | | --- | --- | --- | | 液态玻璃 | 白釉高光 + 模糊 + 厚玻璃折射；关掉 = 平实心气泡 | 开 | | 周边信息同步 | 上面那七处周边信息是否同材质 | 开 | | 气泡不透明度 | 关闭液态玻璃时的底色浓度 | 60% | | 玻璃底色浓度 | 玻璃挡下的底色浓度，越高越不透 | 50% | | 雾化 | 玻璃的模糊半径 | 3px | | 玻璃颜色 | 6 个预设色块 + 取色器自定义 | #ffffff（深色 #12141a） | | 白釉强度 | 表面高光与边缘折射强度，0–200% | 100% | | 深色单独设置 | 打开后深色主题用另一套上面四项 | 关 | 值保存在浏览器本地 `localStorage["dsh-assistant-bubble:settings"]`（清缓存会回默认值）。 ## 兼容性 - **不声明 `engines` / `peerDependencies`**：安装与启用不会被版本检查拦下。 - 客户端半区**不声明** `dsh.client.inject`：模块无条件加载，气泡样式一定生效； `slots` / `locale` 两个服务用 `ctx.inject` 运行时等待，拿不到只丢设置页。 - 唯一外部依赖是宿主写在 DOM 上的语义属性与 CSS-Module 类名后缀。宿主大版本更新后最坏的情况是 **样式静默失效**（看起来像没装），不会报错、不会牵连其它插件。 ## 实现要点 所有参数走 CSS 变量，设置页把值内联写到 `body` 上： ``` --dab-solid-alpha 实心气泡底浓度 --dab-glass-alpha 玻璃挡底浓度 --dab-glass-color 玻璃色（r, g, b） --dab-blur 雾化半径 --dab-sheen 白釉强度倍数 ``` 玻璃配方对齐 [`dsh-plugin-wallpaper-engine`](https://github.com/elysia395/dsh-wallpaper-engine) 的玻璃面： 白釉渐变 + `blur() saturate(1.3) brightness(1.04)` + 双向内阴影折射 + 落地阴影。 ### 思考面板的标题行 展开「思考」时，宿主会给面板内部的**粘性标题行**铺一层实心底色（`--dsw-alias-bg-base`，深色主题下近黑， 展开后就是压在内容上的一条黑带）。这里把它换成**同一颜色的半透明版**并保留吸顶： ```css background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--dsw-alias-bg-base) 80%, transparent) ``` 滚到顶部时仍能遮住下方内容，但不再是一条实心黑条。（不用 `backdrop-filter`：那会把下方的浅色文字 糊成一条白带。） ### 挂在哪些锚点上 | 位置 | 锚点 | | --- | --- | | 助手回复正文 | `[data-chat-flow-kind="assistant-step"] div[class*="_root"] > div[class*="_body"]` | | 工具条（复制 / 点赞 / 用量 / 时间） | `[data-turn-tail] [class*="_actions"]` | | 过程折叠行「已完成，用时 N 秒」 | `[data-turn-process]` | | 过程分组头「正在分析请求 · ⋯」 | `[data-process-activity]` | | 思考触发条 | `[data-turn-trigger]` | | 工具调用行（运行命令 / 网页获取…） | `[data-tool] [data-disclosure-row]` | | 「思考」行 | `[data-variant="think"] [data-disclosure-row]` | | 会话统计行「N 轮 M 步 · tok/s」 | `[data-composer-stats]` | | 上下文占用环「41%」 | `button[class*="_trigger"]:has(> svg[viewBox="0 0 14 14"])` | | 运行行「深度求索中⋯」 | `[data-chat-running]` | | 宽表格 | `.md-table-wide` | ## 开发 实现细节、设计取舍与踩过的坑见 [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)。 ## License MIT

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-composer-launcher

**One "+" panel for compositions, plugins and MCP.**

> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.

> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** This is a **pure UI plugin with no server-side seam at all** — it never rewrites requests, tool results or the system prompt, so the "functional collision" layer does not apply. All **four** client slots it takes are `list` / `keyed`, never `chain`. See [Compatibility](#compatibility).

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-4c6ef5.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Host](https://img.shields.io/badge/host-desktop%20%7C%20web-2f9e44.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility)

**The composer's `+` button, turned into a real menu.**

---

## Table of contents

- [What this is](#what-this-is)
- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
- [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)
- [Settings](#settings)
- [HTTP routes](#http-routes)
- [Interface language](#interface-language)
- [🔗 Integration](#-integration)
- [Known limitations (stated plainly)](#known-limitations-stated-plainly)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
- [Self-check](#self-check)
- [License](#license)

---

## What this is

By default the `+` button left of the composer opens a file picker. Everything else you may want to point the model at — a browser tab you are looking at, an earlier conversation, a skill, an MCP server, one of the plugins installed on this machine — has to be typed by hand, or referenced with `@`.

`dsh-composer-launcher` replaces that button with a **three-group menu**:

| Group | What is in it |
|---|---|
| **Add** | files and folders, earlier chats, plan mode, goal mode |
| **Capabilities** | slash commands, skills, MCP servers |
| **Common plugins** | one row per installed plugin, plus an "all plugins" row |

What you pick does not get pasted in as text. It becomes a **reference chip** on a rail above the input box — the same native chip kind the host already renders for `@` references — and only turns into message text when you actually send.

There is also an **optional browser extension** (`DSH Tab Bridge`) which pushes your real browser's tabs to the plugin over a loopback HTTP bridge, so the Tabs row lists the pages you genuinely have open rather than a throwaway debug instance.

---

## What it does

### 1. The `+` menu (three groups)

A 360px panel, opened from the button at the `conversation.input.left` slot.

- **Add** — *Files and folders* (the host's own picker, multi-select, drag-and-drop; falls back to `@` references when the host exposes no folder picker), *Chats* (via `remote.sessionReferenceResolver`; chats only, no files), *Plan*, *Goal*.
- **Capabilities** — *Commands* (whatever the host's slash-command service offers), *Skills* (read live with `ctx.remote.skills.list({ sessionId })`), *MCP* (needs the host's `remote.mcpManager`).
- **Common plugins** — one row per plugin returned by `ctx.remote.pluginInventory.list()`. That list is read from the host on every load, so installing, removing or disabling a plugin is reflected immediately and there is no cache to keep in sync. Three modes decide which rows appear: `pinned`, `frequent`, `mixed` (see [Settings](#settings)).

Every row can be switched off individually from the settings card.

### 2. Reference chips

Picked items land on a rail **above** the input box (`conversation.input.dock`). A chip is `{ label, kind, icon }` plus an optional `url`, where `kind` is one of `web`, `plugin`, `skill`, `mcp`. Clicking the `×` removes it.

Two properties are worth naming, because both were bugs before they were features:

- **A web chip keeps its address.** A page title with no URL is useless to whoever reads the message — the chip carries the URL and the payload includes it.
- **A session reference stays a chip.** Writing a reference back through the plain-text draft API silently downgrades it to body text; the plugin renders it as a chip instead and never round-trips it through the text editor.

Chips are **per session**, so two chat tabs never share a rail.

On send, each chip is serialised into the message with a short marker, so the model can tell a referenced page from an attached file:

| Chip kind | Marker |
|---|---|
| web page | `【参考网页】<title> — <url>` |
| plugin | `【使用插件】<name>` |
| skill | `【技能】<name>` |
| MCP server | `【MCP】<name>` |

> These markers are literal and stay in Chinese in both interface languages. They are part of the text the **model** reads, not interface copy — translating them would change what the model sees.

### 3. Settings card

Registered on the `settings.plugin.item` slot as a card titled **Launcher** — 「启动器」 in the Chinese interface. It is collapsed the first time you open it and remembers that choice. All twelve fields are listed under [Settings](#settings).

### 4. Debug browser (fallback)

The Tabs row can also read tabs over a remote-debugging port from a Chromium process it starts itself. That is what **Launch debug browser** does — and when the extension is staged, the same call attaches it with `--load-extension` and then verifies through the debugging port that it really mounted, so this route needs no manual step at all (see [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)). It stays a fallback rather than the primary path because it only ever sees that one throwaway-profile instance, never the browser you already have open.

### 5. Loopback bridge

The host half owns a small HTTP bridge on `127.0.0.1:43130` (override: `DSH_LAUNCHER_BRIDGE_PORT`) so the extension can push tabs into it. It binds loopback only, yields politely if an older instance already holds the port, and is used for nothing else.

---

## Screenshots

**The `+` menu — Add / Capabilities / Common plugins — with the Tabs row fed by the extension**

![The composer + menu with the Tabs group and the connected extension](screenshots/01-composer-menu-tab-bridge.png)

**The Tabs row reading a real Microsoft Edge window over the bridge**

![Tab list pushed from Microsoft Edge](screenshots/02-tab-list-edge.png)

**The MCP servers the Capabilities group can reference — the row is built from the host's `remote.mcpManager`**

![MCP servers listed by the host](screenshots/03-mcp-servers.png)

**The plugin inventory the Common plugins group is built from, including its "N / M" narrowing counter**

![Plugin inventory with composition filtering](screenshots/04-plugin-inventory.png)

---

## The browser extension

The plugin works without it — the Tabs row simply says the extension is not installed and points at the button. With it, the row lists the tabs of your **everyday browser**.

### Three ways to get it loaded

Chromium will not let anything silently sideload an extension into the browser you use every day. That is a browser security rule with no plugin-side workaround, so the goal is a different one: make every *remaining* step either automatic or one click.

| Route | What happens | Manual steps |
|---|---|---|
| **A — a browser this plugin starts** | The plugin spawns a separate Chromium process with `--load-extension` pointing at the staged copy, then **verifies through the debugging port that the extension really mounted** | none |
| **B — your everyday browser** | The Tabs row offers *Open the extensions page* and *Copy the extension path*, so loading it once is a paste and a "Load unpacked" | one time, ~20 seconds |
| **C — managed machines** | Chromium enterprise policy (`ExtensionSettings` / `ExtensionInstallForcelist`) pointing at a self-hosted, signed CRX plus an HTTPS update manifest | admin rights; **not shipped here** |

**Route A is verified, not assumed.** After launching, the plugin asks the debugging port for its raw target list and looks for *this* extension's own worker (`chrome-extension://<id>/background.js`) rather than "some extensio

plugins.description: Fix for huge, slow-loading, OOM-ing DSH sessions: deletes the dead streaming fragments out of session logs on disk, so the next load is smaller. DeepSeek Harness plugin.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-vacuum

[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-community%20topic-blue)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
[![deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/deepseek--harness-plugin-4b6bfb)](https://github.com/topics/deepseek-harness)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)

> **Topics:** `dsh` · `dsh-plugin` · `deepseek-harness` · `session-cleanup` · `session-log` ·
> `streaming-fragments` · `vacuum` · `prune` · `oom` · `long-session` · `memory-optimization`

**Is your DSH session getting slower every turn, slower to load, and eventually unopenable — or
does it just OOM?**

That is not a feeling. Every token is written twice: the fragments (`assistant/chunk` and the
packed `text-chunks` / `reasoning-chunks` / `tool-call-chunks` rows) are read by nothing, and
they pile up. A 1,813-turn conversation reached **272 MB on disk**, expanded into **8.43 million
objects** when loaded, took **1.29 GB resident**, and died.

This plugin deletes them **on disk** — not hidden, actually deleted — so the next load is
smaller before anything else happens. Same session after one pass: **86.67 MB → 16.99 MB**,
169,795 fragments → 0, and the non-fragment content: **nothing lost** (`dropped=0`).

**You are accumulating this from turn one.** Measured on real sessions, the number of prunable
fragments tracks output tokens at roughly **0.95–0.99 : 1** — eight sessions, from 88 fragments
for a 91-token one-turn chat up to 1,498 fragments for a 1,516-token six-turn one. Nothing reads
them; they are write-only.

**It runs unless you stop it**, but you can look before it touches anything: `dryRun: true`
records what it *would* do and writes nothing. A pass that cannot verify its own output writes
nothing at all. The swap is atomic, and `.orig` is never deleted for you.

- **Live by default.** A fresh install prunes idle logs with no configuration at all. Set
  `enabled: false` to switch it off, or `dryRun: true` to watch without writing.
- **Never touches a session written in the last 2 minutes** (`liveWindowMs`).
- **Verified before it writes.** The pruned log has to satisfy the loader contract, or the
  original file is left exactly as it was.
- **Destructive by design.** The fragment rows are **deleted**. `.orig` is the only backup,
  and it is never removed for you. Read [Destructive by design](#destructive-by-design)
  before enabling it.

**Why not just hide the chunks?** Folding them out of the `session.history` response is a real
fix for the client, and this plugin does not replace it — the two run together. But the OOM does
not happen in the client. It happens when DSH loads the log: the file is read, every row is
parsed, and the chunk rows expand into millions of objects. If the file on disk is still 272 MB,
skipping them in the response does not stop the next load from rebuilding them. The only way to
stop that is to make the file smaller — see
[How this differs from the runtime approaches](#how-this-differs-from-the-runtime-approaches).

---

## Why

A session log is a concatenation of zstd frames holding JSONL rows. Every token a model
streams is written twice: once as a raw delta (`assistant/chunk`, and the packed rows
`text-chunks` / `reasoning-chunks` / `tool-call-chunks`) and once inside the finalised
`assistant/message`. **Nothing reads the fragments.** Replay does not read them, the model is
never fed them — the projection layer does not even know the word `chunks`. They accumulate
because they are write-only.

Measured on the session that motivated this plugin, a 1,813-turn conversation:

| | |
|---|---|
| rows in the log | 224,000 |
| file on disk | 272 MB |
| objects after loading it | 8.43 million |
| resident memory while loaded | 1.29 GB |
| outcome | out of memory |

The file is small enough to sit on disk unnoticed and large enough to kill the process that
loads it. And because every load pays that cost, the session gets slower and eventually
unopenable — while the rows that cause it are provably unused.

After a cleanup, on the very same session:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| session file | 86.67 MB | 16.99 MB |
| fragment rows | 169,795 | 0 |
| non-fragment content | — | **nothing lost** (`dropped=0`) |
| generation speed shown by the UI | visibly slow | **back to normal** |

> ⚠️ **The "generation speed" row is an observation, not a promise, and it is not explained.** ✗
> What was observed: after the fragments were removed and load memory dropped, the generation
> speed reported by the UI recovered. No controlled before/after tok/s reading was taken, so
> this records the symptom only. Do not read a mechanism into it: context size, cache hit rate,
> time of day and the reasoning-effort setting were each suspected and each ruled out by data,
> and this is the only thing that was actually confirmed.

### What the file size costs on the read path (measured 2026-10-15)

Opening or refreshing a conversation pays for reading its log: the multi-frame zstd stream is
decompressed and every row is parsed. That is the server-side cost a page refresh sits on, and
it scales with the fragment rows this plugin exists to remove — so it was measured directly.

60 logs that still had their pre-cleanup `.orig` beside them, i.e. the **same conversation** on
both sides, decompress + `JSON.parse` of every row, median of 3 runs each:

| | |
|---|---|
| fragment rows across the 60 logs | 960,042 → 300,868 |
| total read time across the 60 logs | 62,893 ms → 6,668 ms (**9.4×**) |
| median speedup | **×7.77** (best ×97.5, worst ×0.72) |
| a 15,298-row log | 859 ms → **37 ms** (×23) |
| a 6,293-row log | 331 ms → **18 ms** (×18) |

> **Scope, so the number is not over-read** ✗: this measures **the log read** (decompress +
> parse every row). It does **not** cover projection computation or client-side rendering —
> neither was measured. The ×0.72 case is a log whose pre-cleanup copy is barely larger than
> the current one, so it is noise on a small number, not a regression. Eight further pairs were
> discarded outright because their `.orig` predates later activity, which would have compared
> two different conversation lengths.

## What it does

`startDelayMs` after boot, once:

1. **Scan.** Walk `$DSH_HOME/sessions` for `session.jsonl.zstd`, sort by size, biggest first.
   A file modified inside `liveWindowMs` is `skipped-live` — the plugin never swaps a log
   out from under a session that may be writing to it.
2. **Threshold.** Count fragment rows and their share of all event rows. Below `minChunkRows`
   or below `minRatio`, the file is `below-threshold` and is not touched at all. A few
   hundred kilobytes of fragments is not worth rewriting a log for.
3. **Prune.** Delete the fragment rows, then renumber `seq` and **remap every cross-event
   reference** onto the new numbering — `sourceEventSeqs`, `surfaceOp.start/end`,
   `shadowedSeqs` and `data.shadowedRange`. Events that the remap itself invalidates (a
   `surfaceOp` whose endpoints were dropped, a surface event left without a marker) are
   dropped too, in a fixpoint loop, so the result is consistent rather than almost-consistent.
4. **Self-verify.** The pruned log must satisfy the same contract DSH loads by: contiguous
   `seq` from 0, a marker on every surface event, no dangling references and no reference to
   a later event. Any violation ⇒ `verify-failed` ⇒ **nothing is written** and the log keeps
   its original size. Refusing to shrink a file is always acceptable; writing a file that DSH
   cannot load is not.
5. **Replace atomically.** Copy the original to `<log>.orig` (only if it does not already
   exist), write the new bytes to `<log>.vacuum-tmp`, then `rename` it over the log. A crash
   mid-write leaves the original intact.

The plugin cannot shrink an already-loaded session — it does not need to. Pruning the file
means every *future* load is small, which is where the memory, the stutter and the OOM came
from.

## Running it on demand

The boot run has one practical flaw: it skips anything written inside `liveWindowMs`
(2 minutes by default), which is usually *the session you actually care about*. And until
